text.title: Rung Placement Failure Modes
text.summary: Six ways verification is placed on the wrong rung, each with the observable symptom and the rule that prevents it. Five of the six cost money; the sixth costs trust, which is worse.

failure.symptom: A defect class keeps recurring, is caught late, and each catch costs a review pass. The fix is always "add it to the reviewer's checklist".
failure.cause: A mechanically decidable defect was routed to a model or a human because that instrument was already in the pipeline.
failure.prevention: Ask Q1 first. Our instance: 528 broken `methodology_refs`/`playbook_refs` across 5,744 MDX files (18,107 refs, 69 phantom slugs) were being found by a review agent — rung-3 prices for a defect a ~20-line validator catches on every commit for zero tokens.

failure.symptom: A large test suite is green and has never caught a quality regression. Coverage numbers look fine.
failure.cause: The tests drive a mock whose answer the test itself authored, so they assert plumbing rather than behaviour. Nothing on rung 2 exists.
failure.prevention: Rung 2 is not an enhancement over a passing unit suite; it is a different rung. Measured in `faion-cli/internal/search/`: 14 test files, 2,868 lines, all plumbing — a ranking-quality regression cannot fail that suite today.

failure.symptom: Everyone knows the bypass flag. The gate's findings are skimmed and dismissed rather than read.
failure.cause: A threshold-tuned rung-1 check was given blocking power, produced false positives, and trained the operator to route around it.
failure.prevention: Mark it `exact: false` and it can only flag. A blocking check with false positives costs more than it ever saved, and the cost is paid in the credibility of every other check beside it.

failure.symptom: A release is blocked or approved on "average quality 4.2 vs 4.0". Rerunning the same suite moves the number.
failure.cause: A rung-3 judge was used to produce an absolute score, and the score was thresholded.
failure.prevention: Pairwise, order-swapped, report win/loss/undecided. At κ=0.549 (arXiv:2604.23178, TMLR 2026) a judge is triage; a difference of 0.2 on an invented scale is noise with a decimal point.

failure.symptom: The same defect is caught by eye in session after session. Everyone considers this normal quality work.
failure.cause: Rung H was treated as a permanent home for checks rather than as the place checks are discovered, so nothing was ever pushed down.
failure.prevention: Log every rung-H catch with the rung it was pushed down to. If the answer is "nowhere" twice for the same defect, that is the record telling you to write a validator.

failure.symptom: The pre-commit hook is commented out, or `--no-verify` has become habitual. The team says the hook is "too slow".
failure.cause: A rung-2 or rung-3 check was wired into the hook, so every commit cost minutes and money.
failure.prevention: Hooks carry rung 1 only. Rung 2 belongs nightly and on prompt/corpus/model-pin changes; rung 3 belongs before a release, run deliberately.
